## Context / Problem

Discovered while fixing bug `c49a-225d-2bc0-4478` (`perplexed-jeanlike-kakarikis`). `check_wall_clock_asserts` missed an indirect wall-clock flake: `test_narrow_operation_persists_the_same_bytes_as_the_legacy_sequence` compared bytes from two independently saved `BindingStore` files. Each save stamps `created_at` / `updated_at` through `BindingLifecycle.bind_confirm` -> `_now_iso`; crossing a one-second boundary made the serialized bytes differ even though the test had no direct elapsed-time assertion.

## Prior BLOCKs addressed

Prior reviews correctly rejected a blanket cross-artifact `read_bytes()` / `read_text()` equality rule because timestamp-free byte comparisons also exist and the variable-assignment shape had not been surveyed. This plan narrows the detector and adds a reason-required local escape.

## False-positive survey

Direct call-vs-call equality under `tests/**` currently appears in these cases:

- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_rich_reemit_state.py`: the motivating timestamp flake; already freezes `_now_iso` and should not need an escape.
- Timestamp-free/deterministic comparisons needing exemption or explicit reason markers if newly flagged: `tests/integration/test_comment_echo_reclaim_manifest.py`, `tests/unit/test_fixture_selection_corpus.py`, `tests/unit/test_build_provenance_fixture_scale.py`, `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_fetcher_snapshot.py`, `tests/unit/test_fixture_selection_escape_index.py`, `tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py`, and `tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py`.

Variable-mediated byte/text comparisons currently found under `tests/**` are same-receiver re-read/idempotency checks, not cross-receiver comparisons. Examples: `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/state/test_binding_lifecycle.py`, `test_binding_baseline.py`, `test_binding_repository.py`, `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler/test_reconcile_idempotency.py`, `tests/unit/test_complexity_baseline.py`, and `tests/unit/test_unique_cache_writes.py`. The implementation must therefore resolve variable sources and exempt variable-vs-direct comparisons when both sides refer to the same receiver expression.

## Decision / Scope

Implement a syntactic, conservative proxy rule in `scripts/check_wall_clock_asserts.py`; do not attempt whole-product timestamp provenance analysis.

Rules:

- Fire on `assert left.read_bytes() == right.read_bytes()` / `!=`, and equivalent `read_text()` comparisons, only when the two receiver expressions are structurally different.
- Fire on variables assigned from `read_bytes()` / `read_text()` receivers and later compared with equality/inequality in the same test function only when both compared sides resolve to file-read receivers and those receiver expressions are structurally different.
- Do not fire when the enclosing test freezes `_now_iso` or `utc_now_iso` via `monkeypatch.setattr`.
- Do not fire on same-receiver comparisons, including variable-vs-direct re-reads of the same receiver expression.
- Add a narrow inline escape marker, `# timing: artifact-equality — <reason>`, covering the assert line or the line directly above. A non-empty reason is mandatory. It is only for reviewed deterministic/timestamp-free artifact comparisons or same-source copy checks.
- Annotate existing timestamp-free direct comparisons newly flagged by the checker with specific reasons; leave the motivating frozen-clock test unescaped.

Finding text should say this is a transitive wall-clock flake proxy and recommend freezing the clock, asserting semantic fields, or using the reason-required escape only for proven timestamp-free artifacts.

## Out of Scope

- Product-code timestamp provenance analysis.
- A broad config allowlist or force-style bypass.
- Auditing beyond the survey above and the checker's test suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `tests/unit/test_wall_clock_assert_lint.py` has a RED-first test proving direct equality/inequality between different `read_bytes()` / `read_text()` receivers is flagged without a clock freeze or escape.
- [x] `tests/unit/test_wall_clock_assert_lint.py` has a RED-first test proving variable-assignment comparisons from different file-content receivers are flagged.
- [x] Contrast tests prove same-receiver direct comparisons, same-receiver variable-vs-direct re-reads, `_now_iso` / `utc_now_iso` freezes, and `artifact-equality` escapes are not flagged.
- [x] Escape tests cover both marker placements: assert line and directly preceding line; blank-reason markers still fire.
- [x] Existing upper-bound wall-clock assertion behavior and hang-guard / CI-skip escapes remain unchanged.
- [x] Existing timestamp-free comparisons in the survey either remain unflagged by same-receiver/frozen-clock logic or are annotated with specific `artifact-equality` reasons.
- [x] Verification: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_wall_clock_assert_lint.py` exits zero, followed before push by `make verify` with the worktree venv on `PATH` and GIT_CONFIG_* unset.
